tools.name: stellaris_get_status
tools.description: Retrieves current Stellaris game status (Layer 1 Global Perception in progressive disclosure architecture). Includes session active state, pause state with pause_reason (event / popup / player) and resumes_when_closed, pending_events (the event windows waiting: window_id, kind, event_key, title; answer them with stellaris_get_active_events / stellaris_resolve_event), speed (0-4), date, empire statistics (empire_size, colonies, starbases, naval_capacity), empire resources (stockpile/income/expense/net for all 26 resources), situation_log indicators, council indicators, society indicators, leaders indicators, market indicators (is_galactic_market, market_fee_percent), discoveries indicators (held_relics_count, can_activate_relic), and contacts indicators (known_empires_count, pending_first_contacts_count).

tools.name: stellaris_set_paused
tools.description: Pauses or unpauses the Stellaris game deterministically via native CPauseCommand. To let time pass and stop at the next event, use stellaris_run_until instead of unpausing and polling.

paused.description: True to pause the game, false to resume simulation.

tools.name: stellaris_set_speed
tools.description: Adjusts the game simulation speed using native game speed commands (stellaris_run_until also takes a speed).

tools.name: stellaris_get_active_events
tools.description: Retrieves all currently active pending event windows: window_id, event_key (script id), title, description, and the shown options. Each option carries `effects`, the effect tooltip the game shows on hover (icons rendered as their names, requirement marks as ✓ / ✗); options without immediate effects have none. Hidden options are not listed.

tools.name: stellaris_resolve_event
tools.description: Resolves an active event choice natively on the main game thread by window ID and option index, applying the decision and closing the event dialog. The start screen closes as its button does (fires on_press_begin). The anomaly window's option 0 leaves it be; to research it use stellaris_research_anomalies with the science ship's fleet. Option 0 of the first contact view closes the view.

window_id.description: The unique window ID of the event window (from stellaris_get_active_events).

option_index.description: The `index` of one of the options listed for this window by stellaris_get_active_events (indexes are not contiguous when some options are hidden; others are refused).

tools.name: stellaris_get_notifications
tools.description: Retrieves the active notification queue (top bar message badges), including queue index, notification type name, title key, parameter, and whether it can be clicked.

tools.name: stellaris_open_notification
tools.description: Triggers a left-click on an active top-bar notification by its queue index (0-based) on the main game thread. This opens/expands the notification into an active modal event or anomaly window and removes it from the top-bar queue.

index.description: The queue index of the notification to click and open (from stellaris_get_notifications).

tools.name: stellaris_get_alerts
tools.description: Retrieves all currently active top-bar alerts (CAlertIconsWindow banners in the center top bar), including alert_id (0..65), internal type name, title, description, and hover tooltip.

tools.name: stellaris_open_alert
tools.description: Triggers a native left-click on an active top-bar alert banner by its alert_id on the main game thread. For First Contact alerts (alert_id: 38), this opens the First Contact narrative and stage view.

alert_id.description: The alert ID (0..65) to click and open (from stellaris_get_alerts).

tools.name: stellaris_get_research_state
tools.description: Retrieves the complete research state across all three technological departments (physics, society, engineering), including currently active research (key, name, tier, cost) and candidate card choices (pool of drawn technologies).

tools.name: stellaris_select_research
tools.description: Selects a technology to research for the specified department area from the candidate pool using native CSelectTechCommand. If a technology is already currently being researched in that area, it is automatically and safely cancelled first (preserving accumulated points into stored research) before switching to the new technology.

area.description: The research area (physics, society, or engineering).

tech_key.description: The unique technology key to select and research (e.g. 'tech_fusion_power').

tools.name: stellaris_cancel_research
tools.description: Cancels the currently active technology research in the specified department area using native CCancelTechCommand, preserving accumulated research points into stored research.

area.description: The research area (physics, society, or engineering).

tools.name: stellaris_get_galaxy_overview
tools.description: Galaxy overview (Layer 1): system and hyperlane totals, a topology_version (a cached stellaris_get_galaxy_map topology stays valid while it is unchanged), the player's capital system and owned systems, how many systems the player has each intel level on, surveyed / unsurveyed systems, unclaimed systems bordering the player's space, known empires with the number of their systems the player can see, and unresearched anomalies. Only what the player knows.

tools.name: stellaris_get_galaxy_map
tools.description: Galaxy map around a system (Layer 1.5): every system within `jumps` hyperlane jumps of center_system_id (default: the player's capital system) as table rows [id, name, x, y, owner_id, intel, jumps, flags] plus the hyperlanes between them as [a, b, length] and the names of the owners shown. flags: S surveyed, C colonized, B starbase, F own fleet present, A unresearched anomaly, K claimed by the player, M megastructure, G gateway / wormhole / relay. owner_id is null when the system is unowned or its owner is unknown to the player. Use stellaris_get_system for one system's planets, starbase and fleets.

center_system_id.description: System to center on (default: the player's capital system)

jumps.description: Hyperlane jumps around the center (0-12, default 3)

tools.name: stellaris_get_system
tools.description: One star system (Layer 2) as the player knows it: position, intel level, owner, whether it is fully surveyed, hyperlanes (neighbor id, name, length), the starbase (level) when the owner is known, planets (class, size, owner, colony, surveyed; deposits only on surveyed planets; an unresearched anomaly if the player has discovered one) when intel is medium or better or the planets are surveyed, and fleets (own fleets always with their stance, other fleets only with high intel). With medium intel or in own space also: megastructures (type, owner), bypasses (relay / gateway / wormhole / L-gate with the systems they lead to), astral rifts and debris; archaeological sites the player can see (type, chapter, clues, difficulty). player_claims is the player's claims on the system. unknown_planets counts planets the player cannot see yet.

tools.name: stellaris_move_fleet
tools.description: Orders one of the player's fleets to fly to a star system (native CSendFleetToLocationCommand, a move to the system's centre; the engine plans the route). queue=true appends the move after the fleet's current orders instead of replacing them. Rejected with the engine's reason for stations or immobile fleets. The fleet's new orders show in stellaris_get_fleets on a later call.

fleet_id.description: One of the player's fleet ids

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_cancel_fleet_orders
tools.description: Cancels every order of the given player fleets (native CFleetCancelOrdersCommand: orders cleared, movement stopped). Refused when none of them has an order.

tools.name: stellaris_follow_fleet
tools.description: Orders a player fleet to follow another fleet (native CFollowFleetCommand); attack=true engages the target when it catches up. The game's own order check decides whether it is allowed.

target_fleet_id.description: The fleet to follow (own or a visible foreign fleet)

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_set_fleet_stance
tools.description: Sets a player fleet's stance (native CSwitchFleetStanceCommand): passive (never engages; the path finder avoids danger), aggressive (engages hostiles), evasive (flees combat). A fleet that follows another (e.g. in an armada) keeps the leader's stance. Own fleets' current stance shows in stellaris_get_system.

tools.name: stellaris_fleet_mia
tools.description: Sends player fleets missing in action (native CGoMIACommand): return_home jumps them home (they are unreachable until they arrive), emergency_ftl retreats them from combat. Refused when none of them can go MIA now.

tools.name: stellaris_claim_system
tools.description: Adds or removes the player's claims on a star system (native CAddSystemClaimCommand / CRemoveSystemClaimCommand; claims cost influence and are what a war goal needs to take the system). Refused with the game's reason (not claimable, not enough influence, at war with the owner ...). The current count is player_claims in stellaris_get_system; the map flags claimed systems with K.

count.description: Claims to add (default 1) or remove (default all)

tools.name: stellaris_land_armies
tools.description: Invades a planet: orders a player army fleet (transports with armies, see stellaris_get_armies / stellaris_embark_all_armies) to land on the planet's colony (native CFleetLandArmiesCommand). On an own or friendly planet the armies disembark there instead. Refused with the game's reason (not at war, no armies aboard, planetary shields up ...).

planet_id.description: Target planet (must have a colony)

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_collect_data
tools.description: Orders a player science ship to research a located special project (native CCollectDataFleetOrderCommand): debris analysis (project_id from stellaris_get_system debris / special_projects, or stellaris_get_situation_log) or an event project that must be researched at a place. With system_id instead, every such project of the player in that system. Refused when there is none the fleet can research.

system_id.description: System whose located projects to research (when no project_id)

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_orbit_planet
tools.description: Orders a player fleet to fly to a planet and orbit it (native CFleetOrbitPlanetCommand).

planet_id.description: Planet to orbit (ids from stellaris_get_system)

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_research_anomalies
tools.description: Orders a player science ship to research the discovered anomalies in a system (native CFleetResearchAnomaliesCommand). Refused with the game's reason, e.g. when the system has no anomaly to research. Anomalies show on planets in stellaris_get_system and as flag A on the map.

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_excavate_site
tools.description: Orders a player science ship to excavate an archaeological site (native CExcavateArchaeologicalSiteFleetOrderCommand). Sites the player can see are listed in stellaris_get_system (archaeological_sites). The game refuses when the site has no chapters left or its own conditions reject the fleet.

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_use_bypass
tools.description: Orders a player fleet to jump through a bypass (hyper relay, gateway, wormhole, L-gate; native CUseBypassCommand) to one of the systems it leads to. The fleet first flies to the bypass. Bypasses and their leads_to systems are listed in stellaris_get_system; stellaris_find_path already routes through bypasses the fleet may use.

to_system_id.description: Destination system (one of the bypass's leads_to)

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_explore_bypass
tools.description: Orders a player science ship to explore a bypass such as a natural wormhole or an unexplored gateway (native CExploreBypassCommand), which reveals where it leads.

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_find_systems
tools.description: Finds systems for a purpose, nearest first by hyperlane jumps from from_system_id (default: the capital), using only what the player knows. purpose: 'unsurveyed' (systems not fully surveyed that the science ship can survey now: the survey order's own check decides route, border access and whether anything is left to survey; the rest are counted by the game's reason in not_surveyable), 'outpost' (unowned systems; with a construction ship, can_build and the game's reason come from the build order's own check), 'deposit' (surveyed planets whose deposit key contains `resource`, e.g. 'minerals', 'energy', 'alloys'), 'colonizable' (the expansion planner's list: unowned surveyed planets in systems with medium+ intel, with the game's habitability for species_id (default: the founder species) and the player's modifiers, best first).

species_id.description: colonizable: species to rate planets for (default: the founder species)

fleet_id.description: outpost: the construction ship to check with; unsurveyed: the science ship (default: the first one of that kind)

resource.description: deposit: substring of the deposit key, e.g. 'minerals'

tools.name: stellaris_find_path
tools.description: The route the game's own path finder plans for one of your fleets from where it is now (closed borders, gateways, wormholes and the fleet's FTL as it may use them) and the travel time in days, the same ETA the fleet gets when ordered there: the systems on the way with the arrival day at each and how the fleet gets there (via: hyperlane, or bypass for a gateway / wormhole / L-gate). reachable=false when the game finds no route for that fleet.

fleet_id.description: The player's fleet that would travel (speed, FTL and border access are the fleet's)

tools.name: stellaris_build_outpost
tools.description: Orders a player construction ship to build an outpost (a starbase) in a star system (native CFleetBuildOrbitalStationCommand). Rejected with the game's reason (for example the system is owned, not surveyed, not bordering your space, or influence is short). Candidates: stellaris_find_systems purpose=outpost.

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_get_megastructure
tools.description: One megastructure (Layer 2): type, name, owner, system, planet, an upgrade under way (target, days done, halted) and, for the player's own, the upgrades its view offers: each with the engine's cost (the cost the upgrade charges), possible and the game's reason when not. Megastructure ids come from stellaris_get_system.

tools.name: stellaris_upgrade_megastructure
tools.description: Starts an upgrade of one of the player's megastructures (native CCountryUpgradeMegaStructureCommand, as the megastructure view's upgrade button): pays the cost and begins the next stage. type is one of stellaris_get_megastructure upgrades[].type; it may be omitted when exactly one upgrade is offered. Rejected with the game's reason (cost, a requirement, already upgrading).

type.description: Target stage key from stellaris_get_megastructure upgrades[].type

tools.name: stellaris_get_buildable_megastructures
tools.description: A construction ship's megastructure build menu (CCountry::ListBuildableMegaStructures: first stages and repairs it can start; upgrades of existing ones are stellaris_upgrade_megastructure): each type with its placement and the engine's cost. With system_id also the sites there the game accepts: planets and stars that meet the type's placement rules (placement=planet), or for open-space types (placement=inside_gravity_well / outside_gravity_well: gateways, citadels, seals) points toward each hyperlane neighbour, the way the AI places them; otherwise the game's reason (a construction already under way, cost, a per-system limit).

tools.name: stellaris_build_megastructure
tools.description: Orders a player construction ship to build a megastructure (native CBuildMegaStructureCommand, as the build menu's site pick): at a planet or star (planet_id), or for open-space types at the point toward a hyperlane neighbour (system_id + toward_system_id). The ship travels there and starts the construction site, paying the cost. Sites come from stellaris_get_buildable_megastructures. Rejected with the game's reason.

planet_id.description: placement=planet: a planet or star id from that tool's sites[]

system_id.description: Open-space placement: the system to build in

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_colonize
tools.description: Orders a player colony ship to colonize a planet (native CFleetColonizePlanetCommand). Rejected with the game's reason (for example uninhabitable, not surveyed, outside your borders).

planet_id.description: Target planet id

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_survey
tools.description: Orders a player science ship fleet to survey (native CFleetSurveyDepositHolderCommand): one planet when planet_id is given, otherwise every planet of system_id. The ship travels there first. Rejected with the engine's reason (for example no scientist, already surveyed, no access).

system_id.description: System to survey completely (when planet_id is not given)

planet_id.description: A single planet to survey

queue.description: Append to the current orders instead of replacing them

tools.name: stellaris_get_situation_log
tools.description: Retrieves the detailed situation log state, including active situations (stage progress, monthly change rate, current approach, owner country), the player's special projects (kind, days left, species for species modification / uplift) and the anomalies it has discovered but not researched (planet and anomaly category). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 2) for F1 Situation Log.

player_only.description: Whether to only return situations owned by the player empire (default true). If false, returns all active situations in the galaxy.

tools.name: stellaris_set_situation_approach
tools.description: Selects and adopts an approach for a situation using native CSetSituationApproachCommand (0x417D). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

situation_id.description: The unique ID of the situation (can be 0 or omitted to default to player country's matching situation).

approach_key.description: The approach key string to select/adopt (e.g. 'approach_revolt_do_nothing', 'approach_voidworm_plague_do_nothing').

tools.name: stellaris_get_government
tools.description: Retrieves detailed Government and Council domain state (Layer 2 Detailed Domain Query). Includes Authority (auth_democratic), Government Type (gov_representative_democracy), Origin, Civics (with keys and localized names), Ethics (fanatic/regular with keys and localized names), Ruler leader details (ID, name, class, level, age, ethic), Active Council Agenda (key, localized name, progress, cost, ready flag), and Council Seats (all positions and assigned leader details).

tools.name: stellaris_launch_council_agenda
tools.description: Launches and activates the currently prepared council agenda using native CFinishAgendaCommand (0x2B16/0x38CA). Validates that the active agenda is ready (progress >= cost) before execution. Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

tools.name: stellaris_set_council_agenda
tools.description: Starts a new council agenda via native CSetCouncilAgendaCommand (Layer 3 Action Command). Choose agenda_key from stellaris_get_government available_agendas (only agendas the engine currently accepts are listed). Finish a ready agenda with stellaris_launch_council_agenda.

tools.name: stellaris_get_civics
tools.description: Government civics (Layer 2): adopted civics with their civic point cost, civic points (total/used/free), and every civic the game would accept added now (each checked with the engine's own government validation). Also returns `reform`: can_reform (with the game's reason, e.g. the 20-year reform cooldown), reform_cost_unity and unity_stockpile. Pass civic_key to check one civic: `requirements` lists the civic's own conditions for this empire, one per line with [trigger_yes]/[trigger_no] (ethics, authority, conflicting civics, origin), and `blocked_by` lists every obstacle (civic points, requirements, reform).

civic_key.description: Optional civic key, e.g. 'civic_technocracy', to check just that civic.

tools.name: stellaris_change_civics
tools.description: Reforms the government's civics via native CChangeGovernmentCommand (Layer 3 Action Command), keeping the authority: adds the civics in `add` and removes those in `remove`. Refused when the civics would cost more civic points than the empire has, or when the game rejects the reform: the error carries the game's reason, `reform` (cooldown/unity cost) and `unmet_requirements` per added civic. Any change starts the game's government reform cooldown (20 years), so check stellaris_get_civics first.

add.description: Civic keys to adopt, from stellaris_get_civics available_civics.

tools.name: stellaris_select_leader_trait
tools.description: Picks a level-up trait for a leader via native CAddTraitFromPoolCommand (Layer 3 Action Command). Offered choices are listed per leader as trait_options / trait_upgrade_options with trait_selections_available (stellaris_get_leaders, and council seats in stellaris_get_government). Rejects traits that are not currently offered.

trait_key.description: Trait key from the leader's trait_options or trait_upgrade_options.

tools.name: stellaris_get_traditions
tools.description: Retrieves detailed Traditions and Ascension Perks state (Layer 2 Detailed Domain Query). Includes summary (adopted_trees_count, max_trees_count: 7, unlocked_traditions_count, next_tradition_cost, can_unlock_tradition, ascension_perk_slots_available), adopted_trees (keys, localized names, unlocked_count, is_finished), unlocked_traditions (keys, localized names, tree_key, tree_name), available_trees (keys, localized names, adopt_tradition_key, adopt_tradition_name), and ascension_perks (adopted perks, total_slots: 8, available_slots).

tools.name: stellaris_adopt_tradition
tools.description: Adopts a new tradition tree or unlocks a tradition perk within an adopted tree via native CActivateTraditionCommand (0x37C2). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

tradition_key.description: Tradition key to adopt (e.g. 'tr_expansion_adopt' to adopt the Expansion tree, or 'tr_expansion_reach_for_the_stars' for an individual tradition perk).

tools.name: stellaris_get_edicts
tools.description: Retrieves detailed Edicts domain state (Layer 2 Detailed Domain Query). Includes summary (active_edicts_count, edict_fund), active_edicts (keys, localized names), and available_edicts catalog (keys, localized names, is_active).

tools.name: stellaris_toggle_edict
tools.description: Enables or disables an edict via native CAddEdictCommand (0x2F36) or CRemoveEdictCommand (0x3628). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

enabled.description: True to enable/activate the edict, false to cancel/deactivate it.

tools.name: stellaris_get_leaders
tools.description: Retrieves full leader and recruitment pool details (Layer 2 Domain Deep-Dive in progressive disclosure architecture). Returns summary counts, list of all hired leaders (id, localized name, class, background_job (job held before recruitment), level, age, ethic, assignment_type, target_id, hire_date), and candidate recruitment pool (id, name, class, level, age, hire_cost, ethic).

tools.name: stellaris_hire_leader
tools.description: Recruits a leader candidate from the candidate pool via native engine CHireLeaderCommand (0x4073). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

candidate_id.description: The unique candidate leader ID to recruit (from pool_candidates in stellaris_get_leaders).

tools.name: stellaris_dismiss_leader
tools.description: Dismisses/fires an existing hired leader via native engine CFireLeaderCommand (0x2EB3). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command). Cannot dismiss the empire ruler.

leader_id.description: The unique leader ID to dismiss/fire (from hired_leaders in stellaris_get_leaders).

tools.name: stellaris_assign_leader
tools.description: Assigns a leader to a planetary governorship, fleet/science ship, army, or council seat via native engine CAssignLeaderCommand (0x4076). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

leader_id.description: The unique leader ID to assign.

assignment_type.description: Assignment type: 1 = Planet Governor, 2 = Fleet / Science Ship Commander, 3 = Army General, 6 = Council Seat.

target_id.description: Target ID: Planet ID (for governor), Fleet ID (for fleet commander), Army ID (for general), or Council Seat ID (for councilor).

tools.name: stellaris_get_species
tools.description: Queries species details in the player's empire or across the galaxy (Layer 2 Domain Query in progressive disclosure architecture). Returns founder species, species names, classes/portraits, traits, detailed 9-category rights configurations (citizenship, living standards, military service, slavery, purge, population controls, colonization controls, migration controls, subspecies integration), remaining cooldown days, empire pop counts, and the complete available rights catalog.

mode.description: Query mode: 'empire' (default) returns species present in or governed by the player's empire; 'galaxy' returns all species known in the galaxy.

species_id.description: Optional specific species ID to query. If provided, returns only this species.

tools.name: stellaris_set_species_rights
tools.description: Modifies a species' rights configuration via native engine CSetSpeciesRightCommand (0x3832). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command). Supports categories: 'citizenship', 'living_standards', 'military_service', 'slavery_type', 'purge_type', 'population_controls', 'colonization_controls', 'migration_controls', 'subspecies_integration'.

species_id.description: The unique species ID to modify (e.g. founder species ID from stellaris_get_status or stellaris_get_species).

category.description: The rights category to change: 'citizenship', 'living_standards', 'military_service', 'slavery_type', 'purge_type', 'population_controls', 'colonization_controls', 'migration_controls', or 'subspecies_integration'.

right_value.description: The new right key (e.g. 'citizenship_full', 'living_standard_stratified', 'living_standard_academic', 'military_service_exempt', 'population_control_yes', etc. See available_rights_catalog in stellaris_get_species).

tools.name: stellaris_get_species_modification_info
tools.description: Queries species genetic modification capabilities, points, picks, current traits, and available traits catalog (Layer 2 Detailed Query in progressive disclosure architecture).

species_id.description: Species ID to query modification traits, points, and picks for (from stellaris_get_species).

tools.name: stellaris_create_species_template
tools.description: Creates a new subspecies modification template with custom traits via native engine CCountryCreateSpeciesModTemplate (0x33B1). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

base_species_id.description: The base species ID to derive the new subspecies template from.

name.description: Optional name of the new subspecies template (e.g. 'Homo Sapiens Superior'). If omitted, automatically inherits the base species name.

traits.description: List of trait keys to assign to this template (e.g. ['trait_intelligent', 'trait_rapid_breeders', 'trait_unruly']).

tools.name: stellaris_modify_species_template
tools.description: Modifies an existing subspecies modification template with updated name and traits via native engine CCountryUpdateSpeciesModTemplate (0x33B0). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

template_species_id.description: The existing subspecies template ID to modify.

name.description: Optional updated name for the template. If omitted, retains previous name.

traits.description: Complete updated list of trait keys for this template.

tools.name: stellaris_delete_species_template
tools.description: Deletes an existing owned subspecies modification template via native engine CCountryDeleteSpeciesModTemplate (0x33B2). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

species_id.description: The subspecies template ID to delete.

tools.name: stellaris_apply_species_template
tools.description: Applies a subspecies modification template to pops on owned colonies, initiating a genetic modification special project via native engine CCreateSpeciesModSpecialProjectCommand (0x4645). Implements progressive disclosure (Layer 3 Action Command).

template_species_id.description: The subspecies template ID to apply to population.

colony_ids.description: Optional list of specific colony IDs to apply this template to. If omitted, applies to all owned colonies with matching base species pops.

tools.name: stellaris_get_fleets
tools.description: Queries detailed fleet and fleet template information (Layer 2 Domain Query in progressive disclosure architecture). Returns fleet ID, template ID, fleet name, military power estimate, total actual ships, total quota, reinforceable status, and breakdown of ship design items (design ID, design name like 'Corvette'/'护卫舰', actual count, target quota, deficit, and whether it can be reinforced).

fleet_id.description: Optional specific fleet ID to query. If omitted, returns all fleets in the empire.

include_civilian.description: Whether to include civilian fleets (science ships, construction ships, transports). Defaults to false (military fleets only).

tools.name: stellaris_reinforce_fleet
tools.description: Reinforces a fleet according to its template deficit via native engine CReinforceFleetCommand (0x3B3C). Dispatches shipbuilding orders to available shipyards, deducting alloy/strategic resources natively and incrementing pending queues.

fleet_id.description: The unique ID of the fleet to reinforce (from stellaris_get_fleets).

tools.name: stellaris_set_fleet_template_quota
tools.description: Sets the target ship quota for a specific ship design in a fleet template via native CFleetTemplate modification (base + 0xE14840 / CFleetTemplate::AddDesign). Allows dynamic expansion or reduction of fleet composition.

fleet_id.description: The unique ID of the fleet whose template should be modified.

design_id.description: The ship design ID to modify the quota for (from stellaris_get_fleets designs list).

target_quota.description: The new target quota for this ship design in the fleet template.

tools.name: stellaris_get_ship_designs
tools.description: Your designable ship designs (the hulls the ship designer offers): for each, the hull, sections with every slot (slot_index, slot_name, equipped component or empty), and the required components (reactor, FTL drive, thrusters, sensor, combat computer, aura ... as the hull defines them) as an indexed list. Use the slot and component keys with stellaris_create_ship_design / stellaris_update_ship_design.

design_id.description: Optional specific ship design ID to query detailed information for. If omitted, returns all empire designs.

tools.name: stellaris_get_ship_design_catalog
tools.description: Queries the global component database (CComponentDatabase at base + 0x3156198) and available ship size hulls. Returns component sets, localized names, icons, size variants (small/medium/large/aux/core), and standard hull sizes.

unlocked_only.description: Whether to only return components currently unlocked by the player empire (default true).

tools.name: stellaris_get_component_details
tools.description: Queries full native in-memory live attributes for a ship component or component set (from Clausewitz CComponentDatabase / CComponentSetTemplate / CComponentTemplate). Matches by component_key (e.g. 'PERDITION_BEAM_ION', 'SMALL_PLASMA_3', 'LARGE_ARMOR_5') or set_key (e.g. 'PERDITION_BEAM', 'PLASMA_3', 'DARK_MATTER_DEFLECTOR'). Returns all size variants in the series (small, medium, large, titanic, aux, etc.) with exact native attributes: min/max damage, range, cooldown, accuracy, tracking, shield/armor/hull multipliers, penetration, windup intervals, power, shield/armor/hull points, regen, evasion/speed modifiers, sensor ranges, ship behavior, and empire tech unlock status.

tools.name: stellaris_create_ship_design
tools.description: Creates a new ship design the way the game's ship designer saves one (native CCreateOrUpdateShipDesignCommand): it starts from your existing design of the hull, applies the slot and required-component changes, and is checked by the game's own rules (component fits the slot, allowed on this hull, technology researched, required components, power). Refused with the reason otherwise. The name must be new, and the result must differ from every design you have (an identical design would replace it). The new design and its id appear in stellaris_get_ship_designs on the next call.

ship_size.description: The customizable hull size for the new ship design (e.g. 'corvette', 'military_station_small', 'destroyer', 'cruiser').

name.description: Name of the new design (unique among your designs; a name list key such as 'HUMAN1_SHIP_Cobra' is localized, anything else shown as typed).

section_name.description: Section name (e.g. 'bow', 'mid', 'stern') to disambiguate slot across sections.

slot_index.description: 0-based slot index within the ship's section.

slots.description: Optional initial list of slot modifications to equip on the newly created design.

core_components.description: Required components to put in (reactor, FTL drive, thrusters, sensor, combat computer, aura ...), as component keys; each replaces the design's required component of the same kind (e.g. ['SENSOR_3', 'CORVETTE_FUSION_REACTOR']).

tools.name: stellaris_update_ship_design
tools.description: Changes components of one of your ship designs the way the game's ship designer re-saves it (native CCreateOrUpdateShipDesignCommand, with the same checks as stellaris_create_ship_design). The game stores the result as a new design with a new id that replaces this one (same name) and refits fleet templates that used it. Renaming is not supported.

design_id.description: The unique ID of the ship design to customize (from stellaris_get_ship_designs).

name.description: The design's current name (renaming is not supported).

section_name.description: Section name (e.g. 'bow', 'mid', 'stern') to disambiguate slot across sections.

slot_index.description: 0-based slot index within the ship's section.

slots.description: List of slot modifications to apply.

core_components.description: Required components to put in (reactor, FTL drive, thrusters, sensor, combat computer, aura ...), as component keys; each replaces the design's required component of the same kind (e.g. ['SENSOR_3', 'CORVETTE_FUSION_REACTOR']).

tools.name: stellaris_upgrade_fleet
tools.description: Orders a military fleet to refit and upgrade to the latest ship designs via native engine command CFleetUpgradeDesignCommand (Opcode 0x2F93). The fleet automatically moves to the nearest available shipyard starbase to carry out refit orders.

fleet_id.description: The unique ID of the fleet to upgrade (from stellaris_get_fleets).

starbase_id.description: Optional specific starbase ID to refit at. Default is 0xFFFFFFFF (nearest available shipyard starbase).

target_design_id.description: Optional specific target design ID to upgrade to. Default is 0xFFFFFFFF (upgrade all ship designs in the fleet).

tools.name: stellaris_delete_ship_design
tools.description: Deletes an obsolete or unused ship design from the empire via native engine command CRemoveShipDesignCommand (Opcode 0x31B2).

design_id.description: The unique ID of the ship design to delete.

tools.name: stellaris_get_market
tools.description: Retrieves current galactic/internal market state (Layer 2 Domain Perception) settled in trade value. Returns galactic market status, current market fee percentage, settlement currency ('trade'), all unlocked tradable commodities (including energy, minerals, food, consumer goods, alloys, and unlocked strategic resources like volatile motes; with stockpiles, batch sizes, unit base price, buy price with fee, and sell price with fee), and active monthly trades.

tools.name: stellaris_market_trade
tools.description: Executes an instant spot trade (buy or sell) on the market via native engine command CMarketBuyResourceCommand / CMarketSellResourceCommand.

units.description: Amount of resource units to trade (rounded to resource batch units). Default: 1 batch.

tools.name: stellaris_set_monthly_trade
tools.description: Creates or cancels a recurring monthly market trade order (Layer 3 Directive Intervention) via native engine command CAddMonthlyTradeCommand / CRemoveMonthlyTradeCommand. Existing orders and their order_id are listed by stellaris_get_market (monthly_trades).

resource.description: Resource key (e.g., 'alloys', 'minerals', 'energy'). Required when creating an order.

amount.description: Monthly quantity in units (e.g., 10, 50, 100). Required when creating an order.

price_limit.description: Maximum unit price in trade value (e.g. 100). Optional, 0 for no limit.

cancel.description: Set to true to cancel an existing order identified by order_id. Default: false.

order_id.description: Required when cancel is true: order_id from stellaris_get_market monthly_trades.

tools.name: stellaris_get_discoveries
tools.description: Retrieves relics, astral actions, and minor artifact actions (Layer 2 Domain Perception). Includes player held relics with passive/triumph descriptions and activation status, all galaxy relics, astral actions, and artifact actions.

tools.name: stellaris_activate_relic
tools.description: Activates the triumph effect of an owned relic (Layer 3 Directive Intervention) via native engine command CActivateRelicCommand (Opcode 0x3CEA).

tools.name: stellaris_get_contacts
tools.description: Retrieves galactic contacts and diplomatic communications (Layer 2 Domain Perception). Lists all known empires, contact flags, diplomatic treaties (commercial pact, research agreement, migration pact), and pending first contact logs. NOTE: Claims (宣称) are excluded.

tools.name: stellaris_get_outliner
tools.description: Retrieves the macro summary of the empire's Outliner (Layer 1 Progressive Disclosure). Summarizes counts and KPI indicators across the 4 key categories: Sectors/Colonies (total sectors, total colonies, total pops, capital system, and sector catalog with sector_id/name/KPI), Military Fleets (combat fleets count, total military power), Civilian Fleets (civilian fleets count), and Armies (garrison armies count, transport armies count). NOTE: Uncolonized / colonizing planets without definitive sector assignment are excluded.

tools.name: stellaris_get_sectors
tools.description: Expands a specific sector or all sectors to inspect member colonies (Layer 2 Progressive Disclosure). Provide 'sector_id' (from stellaris_get_outliner; colonies in no sector are grouped with sector_id null). If omitted, expands all sectors. Returns colony_id (the colony) and planet_id/id (use it for planet tools), name, system name, population, size, capital status, colonizing progress, current construction (building/district and progress), and the planet status alerts the game's outliner shows: crisis states (blockaded = under orbital bombardment, with the blockading empire and its bombardment stance; occupied) and notices (construction slot, capital upgrade, unemployment, excess civilians, overcrowding, low stability, clearable blocker).

sector_id.description: Sector id to expand (from stellaris_get_outliner). If omitted, expands all sectors.

tools.name: stellaris_get_military_fleets
tools.description: Retrieves detailed list of all military combat fleets (Layer 2 Progressive Disclosure). Includes fleet ID, fleet name, military power rating, current ship count, template quota, reinforcement capability, and current operational status.

tools.name: stellaris_get_civilian_fleets
tools.description: Retrieves list of all civilian ships and non-combat fleets (Layer 2 Progressive Disclosure). Categorizes science ships, construction ships, and colony ships with fleet ID, ship name, and operational status.

tools.name: stellaris_get_armies
tools.description: Retrieves list of ground armies and transport fleets (Layer 2 Progressive Disclosure). Distinguishes planetary garrison armies from embarked transport fleets, including army ID, type/name, combat strength power, health percentage, and stationed planet ID/name.

tools.name: stellaris_get_planet_details
tools.description: Retrieves comprehensive planetary details for a specific colony in Stellaris 4.5.0 Cygnus (Layer 3 Progressive Disclosure Entity Deep-Dive). Fully aligned with Stellaris 4.5.0 Districts & Zones mechanics: 1) Planet overview (planet type, habitability %, colony date, planet size); 2) Top KPI bar (stability %, pop groups scale e.g. 5.9K, pop capacity, crime %, housing, amenities, unemployed, pop growth); 3) 4 Primary Districts (City, Generator, Mining, Agriculture) with their respective Zone Specializations, zone slots, unlock requirements, and buildings; 4) Monthly resources from the colony's own economy tables: produced, upkeep and net per resource (non-zero only); 5) Active construction queue; 6) Planetary features (all natural deposits and blockers with clear time, clear costs, modifiers, swap unlock types, and queued clearance status); 7) Current population breakdown (species list with pop counts, display '5.9K', share %, net change, portrait); 8) Monthly population summary (net change, growth, migration, assembly, categories, demographic pie chart); 9) Colony ascension (tier 0-10, designation multiplier +25%/tier, can_ascend, status text); 10) Colony status alerts, identical to the outliner: blockaded (orbital bombardment; name carries the blockader, desc the bombardment stance), occupied, construction_available, upgrade_available, unemployment, excess_civilians, overcrowding, low_stability, blocker_available. Species ids are the full ids used by the species tools.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to inspect (obtainable from stellaris_get_sectors or stellaris_get_outliner).

tools.name: stellaris_set_district_zone
tools.description: Queues a zone into a district's zone slot (native construction queue, CBuildableZone), replacing the zone there. Rejected with the game's reason when the zone is not allowed in that slot. Get district ids, slots and allowed zones from stellaris_get_available_district_zones.

planet_id.description: Planet id

slot.description: Zone slot index of that district

tools.name: stellaris_get_available_district_zones
tools.description: Zone slots of a colony's districts (Layer 2): per district (id, type) and slot, the zone currently there and every zone type the game would queue into that slot (the construction queue's own validation of a CBuildableZone), with cost and build days. include_blocked=true also lists the refused zone types with the game's reason. Build one with stellaris_set_district_zone.

planet_id.description: Planet id (from stellaris_get_sectors or stellaris_get_outliner).

district_type.description: Optional district type filter (e.g. 'district_city' or 'city'); empty for all.

include_blocked.description: Also list zone types the game refuses, with the reason

tools.name: stellaris_cancel_construction
tools.description: Removes one item from a construction queue (native CRemoveBuildableFromQueueCommand, as the queue's cancel button): a building, district or zone on a planet (get_planet_details construction_queue) or a ship at a shipyard (stellaris_get_buildable_ships queue). Refunds as the game does.

tools.name: stellaris_get_buildable_ships
tools.description: Ships a starbase's shipyard can build now (Layer 2): every design of the empire (science, construction and colony ships as well as warships), each checked with the engine's own construction validation, with cost after the empire's modifiers and build_days. Pass design_id to check one design and get the game's reason when it cannot be built. To keep military fleets topped up, the fleet manager (stellaris_set_fleet_template_quota / stellaris_reinforce_fleet) is the better tool.

starbase_id.description: The starbase whose shipyard builds the ship.

system_id.description: Or the system of that starbase (e.g. the capital system).

species_id.description: Colony ships: the species to check with (default: the founder species).

tools.name: stellaris_build_ship
tools.description: Queues ships of a design at a starbase's shipyard (native CAddBuildableToQueueCommand with the engine's ship buildable, as the starbase view's Build button): science, construction and colony ships (colony ships carry species_id, default the founder species), or single warships. Refused with the game's reason (no shipyard, resources, tech, ...). For building warships in bulk, use the fleet manager instead (stellaris_set_fleet_template_quota, then stellaris_reinforce_fleet): it plans and queues them for you.

starbase_id.description: The starbase whose shipyard builds the ship.

system_id.description: Or the system of that starbase (e.g. the capital system).

species_id.description: Colony ships: the species that settles (default: the founder species), as the game's species dialog asks.

tools.name: stellaris_get_buildable_districts
tools.description: Districts the game accepts on a planet now (Layer 2), each checked with the engine's own construction validation (planet size, free district capacity, tech, resources). Returns current[] (district types on the colony with their count) and buildable[] (key, name, built, cost after the empire's modifiers, build_days). Pass district_key to check one type: can_build, or the game's reason.

planet_id.description: Planet ID (planet_id from the outliner or get_planet_details).

district_key.description: Optional district type key to check one type (can_build, or the game's reason).

tools.name: stellaris_build_district
tools.description: Queues one more district of a type on a planet (native CAddBuildableToQueueCommand with the engine's CBuildableDistrict, as the planet view builds it). Refused with the game's reason when it cannot be built.

planet_id.description: Planet ID (planet_id from the outliner or get_planet_details).

tools.name: stellaris_demolish_district
tools.description: Demolishes one district of a type on a planet (native CDestroyDistrictCommand). Refused with the game's reason when the game does not allow it.

planet_id.description: Planet ID (planet_id from the outliner or get_planet_details).

tools.name: stellaris_get_buildable_buildings
tools.description: Buildings the game accepts in each building zone of a planet now (Layer 2), each checked with the engine's own construction validation. Per zone: zone_id, zone key/name, district, buildings/max_buildings, and buildable[] with cost (after the empire's cost modifiers) and build_days. Pass building_key to check one building in every zone (can_build, or the game's reason), and zone_id to limit to one zone.

planet_id.description: Planet ID (planet_id from the outliner or get_planet_details).

building_key.description: Optional building key to check, e.g. 'building_foundry_1'.

tools.name: stellaris_build_building
tools.description: Queues construction of a building (native CAddBuildableToQueueCommand with a CBuildableBuilding), validated by the engine; the game's reason is returned when refused. slot_index is the target zone id (see stellaris_get_buildable_buildings); without it the first zone that accepts the building is used.

planet_id.description: Planet ID to construct the building on.

slot_index.description: Optional target zone id (zone_id from stellaris_get_buildable_buildings / districts[].zones[].slot_index). Zone ids differ per planet.

tools.name: stellaris_upgrade_building
tools.description: Upgrades an existing building on a planet in Stellaris 4.5.0 Cygnus via native CBuildableUpgradeBuilding entity and CAddBuildableToQueueCommand. Automatically resolves the building's current slot/zone and target upgrade definition if omitted.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 11 for Earth).

building_id.description: Unique instance ID (bid) of the existing building to upgrade (e.g. 2, 3, 16777308, 1).

upgrade_to_key.description: Optional target upgrade building key (e.g. 'building_hyper_entertainment_forum', 'building_commercial_megaplex', 'building_physics_lab_2', 'building_factory_2'). If omitted, will be inferred from the existing building type.

tools.name: stellaris_get_clearable_blockers
tools.description: Retrieves all planetary deposit blockers (e.g. Great Pacific Garbage Patch, Failing Infrastructure, Decrepit Dwellings, Deep Sinkhole) on a specified planet/colony. Evaluates real-time clearance status using native game engine validation (can_clear, is_queued, prerequisites, and resource affordability).

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to inspect blockers for (e.g. 11 or 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_clear_blocker
tools.description: Queues a deposit blocker clearance order on a planet via native CBuildableClearDepositBlocker entity and CAddBuildableToQueueCommand. Enforces strict engine validation of technology prerequisites, resource costs, and queue availability before dispatching to the main thread.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID where the blocker is located (e.g. 11 or 3 for Earth).

deposit_id.description: Unique instance ID of the deposit blocker to clear (obtainable from stellaris_get_clearable_blockers, e.g. 309, 310, 311).

deposit_key.description: Blocker definition key (e.g. 'd_great_pacific_garbage_patch', 'd_failing_infrastructure_earth', 'd_decrepit_dwellings'). Can be used instead of deposit_id.

tools.name: stellaris_get_planetary_decisions
tools.description: Queries planetary decisions for a given planet or colony. Evaluates native engine enactment preconditions (technologies, resources, cooldowns, planet features) via CEnactDecisionCommand::IsValid, returning the list of available decisions with localized names, durations, and can_enact status.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to query decisions for (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_enact_planetary_decision
tools.description: Enacts a planetary decision on a colony using native engine command CEnactDecisionCommand. Enforces strict engine validation of conditions, resources, and prerequisites before dispatching to the main thread.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to enact the decision on (e.g. 3 for Earth).

decision_key.description: Key or alias of the decision (e.g. 'decision_planet_luxuries_boost', 'decision_planet_food_boost', 'decision_discourage_growth', 'decision_mastery_of_nature', 'luxuries', 'food').

tools.name: stellaris_get_terraforming_options
tools.description: Queries the current terraforming state and available terraforming target options for a planet from the global CTerraformDatabase. Returns ongoing terraforming progress (progress days, total days, remaining days, percentage) if active, and all valid target planetary classes with duration and can_terraform readiness.

planet_id.description: Planet ID to query terraforming options for (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_start_terraforming
tools.description: Initiates planetary terraformation project using native engine command CStartTerraformationCommand. Enforces full prerequisite validation (technologies such as Climate Restoration / Terrestrial Sculpting, energy credits stockpile) before dispatching to the game thread.

planet_id.description: Planet ID to terraform (e.g. 3 for Earth).

target_class.description: Target planetary class key or alias (e.g. 'pc_ocean', 'pc_tropical', 'pc_gaia', 'pc_desert', 'ocean', 'gaia').

link_index.description: Unique index of the terraforming link from CTerraformDatabase (obtainable from stellaris_get_terraforming_options). Can be provided instead of target_class.

tools.name: stellaris_cancel_terraforming
tools.description: Cancels an ongoing planetary terraforming project on a planet using native engine command CCancelTerraformationCommand. Restores energy credits and resets the planetary terraforming state.

planet_id.description: Planet ID where terraforming is to be cancelled (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_get_planetary_features
tools.description: Retrieves all planetary features and blockers for a specific planet in Stellaris 4.5.0 Cygnus. Includes complete natural features, deposit blockers, queued clearance orders, clearance times (days), resource clearing costs (e.g. 300 energy), modifier effects (e.g. planet_max_districts_add, generator/mining/farming district capacity bonuses), and on-clear swap replacements (e.g. unlocking Delhi Sprawl).

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to inspect (obtainable from stellaris_get_sectors or stellaris_get_outliner).

tools.name: stellaris_ascend_colony
tools.description: Ascends a colony to the next planetary ascension tier (1-10) using native engine command CIncreasePlanetaryAscensionTierCommand. Increases planetary designation efficiency bonus by +25% per tier. Validates prerequisites (traditions unlocked, unity cost) before dispatching.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to ascend (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_get_planet_jobs
tools.description: Retrieves detailed job and workforce allocation for a colony in Stellaris 4.5.0 Cygnus (Layer 2 Progressive Disclosure). Returns jobs categorized by stratum (ruler, specialist, worker, civilian), detailing current workforce, max workforce capacity, bonus workforce, effective workforce, workforce limit, whether prioritized (favorite), and whether it can be prioritized.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to inspect (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_set_job_priority
tools.description: Toggles or sets the priority (favorite) status for a job type on a planet using native engine command CSetFavoriteJobCommand. Prioritized jobs receive preferential workforce allocation from available pops.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_set_job_workforce_limit
tools.description: Adjusts the workforce limit slider for a specific job on a planet using native engine command CChangeJobWorkforceLimitCommand. Allows capping or reopening workforce capacity for specific jobs (e.g. 0 to disable, or -1 for max capacity).

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 3 for Earth).

limit.description: Workforce allocation limit (non-negative integer count, or -1 for uncapped maximum capacity).

tools.name: stellaris_get_planet_armies
tools.description: Retrieves complete army information for a planet/colony in Stellaris 4.5.0 Cygnus (Layer 2 Progressive Disclosure). Returns overview (stationed armies count, garrison power, assault power, deploy_in_orbit, include_in_builder), stationed armies list (army_id = full id accepted by disband, engine-rendered name, type_key, is_defense, is_occupation, power as computed by the game, health/max_health, morale/max_morale for types with morale, species), recruitable army types catalog (build time and the type's health/damage/morale/morale-damage multipliers), and current army recruitment queue.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID to inspect (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_set_planet_army_settings
tools.description: Controls planet army status settings in Stellaris 4.5.0 Cygnus. Toggles or sets '部署到轨道上' (deploy_in_orbit) via CToggleDeployArmiesInOrbitCommand and/or '包含在陆军建造功能中' (include_in_builder) via CToggleIncludeInArmyBuilderCommand.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 3 for Earth).

deploy_in_orbit.description: Whether recruited armies should automatically deploy into orbit (true) or stay stationed on the surface (false).

include_in_builder.description: Whether this planet is included in the empire army builder roster (true) or excluded (false).

tools.name: stellaris_embark_all_armies
tools.description: Embarks all stationed assault armies from a colony into orbit as a transport fleet using native engine command CMoveArmyToOrbitCommand ('全部登船'). Defense armies remain on the planet.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 3 for Earth).

tools.name: stellaris_disband_planet_army
tools.description: Disbands a specific army stationed on a planet using native engine command CDisbandArmyCommand.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 3 for Earth).

army_id.description: Unique army ID / handle slot to disband.

tools.name: stellaris_recruit_planet_army
tools.description: Recruits an assault army on a colony into the planet's recruitment queue (Queue 1) using native engine command CAddBuildableToQueueCommand with CBuildableArmy.

planet_id.description: Planet / Colony ID (e.g. 3 for Earth).

army_key.description: Army type key from catalog to recruit (e.g. 'assault_army', 'xenomorph_army', 'clone_army', 'gene_warrior_army').

species_id.description: Optional species ID for the recruited army pops (defaults to colony founder/dominant species).

tools.name: stellaris_list_saves
tools.description: Save games on disk (Layer 1, read from the save files' headers; the game is not touched). Without campaign: every campaign folder, newest first, with its number of saves and its newest save's empire name, game date and ironman flag, plus continue (the save the main menu's Continue opens). With campaign: that campaign's saves, newest first, each with game version, empire name, game date and ironman. Load one with stellaris_load_game.

campaign.description: A campaign folder from the list without campaign

tools.name: stellaris_load_game
tools.description: Loads a save, from the main menu or from inside a game (which is left for the main menu first, as the game does). Without arguments it continues: the save the main menu's Continue button opens (else the newest save). With campaign only: that campaign's newest save. With campaign and file: that save (stellaris_list_saves). The result's source says which rule picked it (continue; newest when Continue's save no longer exists). By default it waits until the game is loaded (screen in_game) and closes the start screen, so the next call can play; wait=false only starts the load (follow it with stellaris_get_status: screen loading -> in_game). The game refuses a save made for another version or other DLCs: the main menu stays and the tool says so.

file.description: Save file in that campaign, with or without .sav

wait.description: Wait until the game is loaded (default true)

tools.name: stellaris_save_game
tools.description: Saves the current game into its campaign folder (as the game's save menu; a local save). The file is written over the next moments; the result says when it is on disk. A name that exists is refused unless overwrite is set.

name.description: File name without .sav (default: the game date, e.g. 2354.07.01)

overwrite.description: Replace a save of the same name

tools.name: stellaris_exit_to_main_menu
tools.description: Leaves the current game for the main menu (as the in-game menu's resign/exit; an ironman game is saved first, any other is not: save with stellaris_save_game before). Waits until the main menu is shown unless wait=false.

wait.description: Wait until the main menu is shown (default true)

tools.name: stellaris_list_empire_designs
tools.description: The empires a new game can be played as (Layer 1): the prescripted empires and the user's saved designs, each with its key, name, type (prescripted / user), species name, ethics, origin and playable (the design's own playable condition), and on the main menu valid (the game's validation for playing it; the game's empire list hides prescripted designs that fail either). Works on the main menu and in game. Details and why a design is invalid: stellaris_get_empire_design.

tools.name: stellaris_get_empire_design
tools.description: One empire design in full (Layer 2): names, species (class, portrait, names, name list, gender, traits) and a secondary species when it has one, ethics, authority, government, civics, origin, home world (planet class, names, system initializer), ship prefix, ship and city sets, room, advisor voice, and for a user design its spawn setting. On the main menu also valid and, when not, invalid_reason: the game's own validation for playing it (IsEmpireDesignValid, the check the empire list and the empire editor use, with their messages).

tools.name: stellaris_get_empire_design_text
tools.description: One empire design as game script (Layer 2): the block the game reads it from, out of the user design file or the game's prescripted_countries. Edit it and pass it as text to stellaris_save_empire_design for what the structured changes do not cover (secondary species, ruler, flag, playable conditions ...).

tools.name: stellaris_save_empire_design
tools.description: Create or edit a user empire design (Layer 2 write, main menu). Starts from base (any design, prescripted or user; by default key itself when that is a user design, edited in place) with changes applied, or from the full script in text (stellaris_get_empire_design_text). The game reads the result the way it reads its user design file, runs its fix-ups and its validation (IsEmpireDesignValid, the empire editor's check); only a valid design is kept, and it is written into the user design file without rewriting the other designs. validate_only: check, do not save. Returns the design's summary, valid, invalid_reason (the game's text), saved, and the script that was checked.

key.description: Key of the design to save (a new key creates one; a prescripted empire's key is refused)

base.description: Design to start from (default: key, when it is a user design)

species_class.description: Species class key, e.g. HUM, MAM, ROBOT

portrait.description: Portrait key of that class, e.g. human

gender.description: Species gender: male, female, indeterminable or not_set

traits.description: All the species' trait keys: replaces the list, so keep its organic / robotic trait (e.g. trait_organic)

planet_class.description: Home planet class key, e.g. pc_continental

initializer.description: Home system initializer key (empty: a random system)

ship_set.description: Ship set (graphical culture) key, e.g. humanoid_01

spawn.description: Spawn this empire as an AI in new games: yes, no, always

ruler_portrait.description: Ruler's portrait key, e.g. human_female_05 (default: one of the species' portrait)

ruler_trait.description: Ruler's starting trait key, e.g. trait_ruler_eye_for_talent

changes.description: Fields to set; a list replaces the whole list

text.description: The design's full script, one block `key = { ... }`, instead of base (changes still apply)

validate_only.description: Check with the game's validation and do not save

overwrite.description: Replace an existing user design with this key (implied when editing it in place)

tools.name: stellaris_delete_empire_design
tools.description: Delete a user empire design (main menu): the game drops it, and its block is removed from the user design file (the file before the change is kept next to it as .mcp_backup). Prescripted empires cannot be deleted.

tools.name: stellaris_get_new_game_options
tools.description: Everything a new game can be set to, in one call (Layer 1): galaxy sizes (template, stars, the empire counts the galaxy setup allows and their defaults) and shapes from the game's map files, the current single-player galaxy settings (null = the size's own value), and the choices of the named settings (difficulty, aggressiveness, crisis_type, scaling, technology_difficulty_scale) with their in-game names. Empires: stellaris_list_empire_designs, or give one inline to stellaris_new_game.

tools.name: stellaris_set_galaxy_settings
tools.description: Set single-player galaxy settings for the next new game (main menu), as the galaxy setup's pickers do: written into the game's settings, which the new game reads. Checked against the galaxy size's limits first; nothing is written when one is wrong. Returns all settings after the change.

settings.description: Galaxy settings by the game's settings-file names (stellaris_get_new_game_options lists them all); null resets one to the galaxy size's value. template (size: tiny, small, medium, large, huge), shape, num_empires (AI empires), num_advanced_empires, num_fallen_empires, num_marauder_empires, num_nomad_empires, num_guaranteed_colonies, colonizable_planet_odds (habitable worlds, 1.0 = normal), primitive_odds, crises (crisis strength), technology / traditions (cost, 1.0 = normal), resource_abundance, num_wormhole_pairs, num_gateways, num_hyperlanes, naval_capacity_mult, mid_game_start / end_game_start / victory_year (years), difficulty (civilian .. grand_admiral), aggressiveness (normal, high, low), crisis_type (any, prethoryn, unbidden, contingency, synth_queen, all), scaling (off, mid, late), technology_difficulty_scale (off, low, normal, high, extreme), advanced_starts_near_player, clustered, ironman, caravaneers_enabled, lgate_enabled ...

tools.name: stellaris_new_game
tools.description: Start a new single-player game in one call (main menu): set the galaxy (galaxy, optional), pick or create the empire (empire), launch, and wait until the game is in (start screen closed, game paused). empire: an existing design's key (stellaris_list_empire_designs), "random" (the game's random empire, the default), or a whole empire inline: { key?, base?, text?, ...the fields of stellaris_save_empire_design's changes }. Without base or text an inline empire starts from the game's defaults, so give every part (species_class, portrait, name_list, traits, ethics, authority, civics, origin, name, species names, ship_set ...). It is saved as a user design (key default mcp_empire, replaced each time) once the game's validation accepts it; when the game refuses it nothing starts and the error carries the game's reason. Galaxy generation takes seconds (tiny) to minutes (huge).

key.description: Design key to save it under (default mcp_empire)

base.description: Design to start from instead of the game's defaults

text.description: Full design script instead of base

empire.description: Design key, "random", or an inline empire

galaxy.description: Galaxy settings by the game's settings-file names (stellaris_get_new_game_options lists them all); null resets one to the galaxy size's value. template (size: tiny, small, medium, large, huge), shape, num_empires (AI empires), num_advanced_empires, num_fallen_empires, num_marauder_empires, num_nomad_empires, num_guaranteed_colonies, colonizable_planet_odds (habitable worlds, 1.0 = normal), primitive_odds, crises (crisis strength), technology / traditions (cost, 1.0 = normal), resource_abundance, num_wormhole_pairs, num_gateways, num_hyperlanes, naval_capacity_mult, mid_game_start / end_game_start / victory_year (years), difficulty (civilian .. grand_admiral), aggressiveness (normal, high, low), crisis_type (any, prethoryn, unbidden, contingency, synth_queen, all), scaling (off, mid, late), technology_difficulty_scale (off, low, normal, high, extreme), advanced_starts_near_player, clustered, ironman, caravaneers_enabled, lgate_enabled ...

wait.description: Wait until the game is in (default true)

tools.name: stellaris_run_until
tools.description: Let game time pass until something needs the player, then return with the game paused. Unpauses (at speed, when given) and stops at the first of: an event window opening (stopped_because "event"), the game pausing itself or being paused ("paused": pause_reason popup / player), the date after days or until_date ("date"), or max_seconds of real time ("time_limit"). Does not start while event windows wait ("pending_events": resolve them first). Returns the dates, days passed, why it stopped and the event windows waiting (details: stellaris_get_active_events).

days.description: Game days to run (30 = a month, 360 = a year)

until_date.description: Run until this game date, YYYY.MM.DD

speed.description: Game speed while running, 0 (slowest) .. 4 (fastest); default: as it is
